fieldissues.issue: The title says GAO found DOGE’s $215 billion claims “fabricated,” which implies intentional falsification; the record describes unsupported or unverifiable estimates. The short repeats the title.

The medium refers to “supplied figures,” and the long calls DOGE’s claims “inflated” without attributing that characterization. These phrases make the account read as editorial judgment rather than a neutral report of GAO’s findings.
Government Accountability Office appears as both a topic and organization tag, while Elon Musk is tagged but not named in the merged text.

proposedchanges.change: Use “GAO Finds DOGE Savings Estimates Unsupported or Incorrect.” Write a distinct summary that attributes the unverifiable grant and lease figures to the GAO review and distinguishes claimed savings from realized savings.

Replace “supplied figures” and “inflated” with attributed wording: GAO found that documentation did not support many claims, some listed contracts had no termination action, and the audit could not verify most grant savings. Do not infer intent from those findings.
Remove Government Accountability Office from topic_tags if it remains in organization_tags. Remove Elon Musk unless the description names his relevant role.

evidencebasis: The assigned GAO audit packet distinguishes claimed savings from actions taken and reports that 96.2% of grant claims could not be verified.
The merged medium explicitly says the findings concern transparency and calculation, not a verified realized-savings total.
The GAO URL is retained; the current tags duplicate GAO across subject and organization fields and include Elon Musk absent from the prose.
notes: The long contains detailed audit results, but the title must not infer fabrication or present claimed savings as established losses or gains.

fieldissues.issue: The title says the SEC “dropped” more than 60% of cases, while the medium and source summary say it eased up through dismissals, pauses, reduced penalties, and other changes. The short repeats the title.

The medium says the linked article could not be retrieved and directs readers to confirm the sample and causal claims. The long describes the retreat as systematically enriching crypto firms and benefiting Trump’s family, a conclusion not established by the count of eased matters.

proposedchanges.change: Use “New York Times Review Finds SEC Eased Up on More Than 60% of Pending Crypto Matters.” Write a separate summary that distinguishes dismissals from pauses and penalty reductions.

Remove the source-retrieval note. Attribute the broad finding to the Times and distinguish case-status changes from causal or financial-benefit conclusions. Keep specific settlement and investment details only as attributed facts, not proof that an investment caused an SEC decision.

evidencebasis: The source metadata identifies a December 2025 New York Times review and says it counted dismissals, pauses, reduced penalties, and other pullbacks under the broader term “eased up.”
The merged medium repeats that broader definition, while the title says cases were dropped.
The merged long asserts direct enrichment and family benefit beyond what the aggregate case-change statistic alone establishes; the Times URL remains in source_urls.
notes: The title should reflect the review’s broad measure. The article-retrieval note and causal conclusions should not appear as settled facts in the reader-facing entry.
